description: MICROFLARE is a team interested in space, technology, data, and science. We bring together Computer Science and Chemical Engineering skills. We are working on fire behaviour in microgravity and fire safety. We are looking for members with skills in Python, AI/ML, data analysis, UI/UX, or scientific research.
summary:
FLARE-X is an interactive web-based research tool designed to explore NASA's BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids-II) microgravity combustion experiment data. It helps users understand how different fuel materials and experimental conditions, such as oxygen percentage and airflow, relate to recorded flame behaviour.

The platform provides interactive dashboards, data filtering, comparison of two experiments, data quality checks, and research notes. It uses Python, Streamlit, Pandas, and Plotly for data processing and visualization, with Supabase for user authentication.

FLARE-X aims to make complex space-based combustion data easier to explore and understand, supporting fire-safety research for future human space missions to the Moon and Mars. It is a research-support tool and does not predict fire risks or prove cause-and-effect relationships.
details:
FLARE-X – Microgravity Fire Intelligence

What does the project do and how does it work?

Fire behaviour in microgravity can differ from fire behaviour on Earth. Understanding these differences is important for protecting astronauts and spacecraft during future missions to the Moon and Mars.

FLARE-X is an interactive web-based platform that helps users explore NASA's BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids-II) microgravity combustion experiment data. It allows users to filter experiment records, visualize data through interactive charts, compare two experiments, and examine data quality.

The platform uses recorded experimental information such as fuel materials, oxygen percentages, airflow conditions, and flame outcomes to make the data easier to understand.

What are its benefits?

  • Makes complex NASA experimental data easier to explore.
  • Helps users compare different combustion experiments.
  • Provides interactive visualizations of experimental conditions and recorded outcomes.
  • Highlights unclear or missing data to support careful interpretation.
  • Brings important research information together in one platform.

What is the intended impact?

FLARE-X aims to support the understanding of microgravity combustion behaviour and contribute to fire-safety research for future human space exploration. It can help students and researchers explore experimental records and identify patterns or questions for further investigation.

What tools and technologies were used?

  • Python – Main programming language.
  • Streamlit – Web application development.
  • Pandas – Data processing and filtering.
  • Plotly – Interactive charts and visualizations.
  • Supabase – User authentication.
  • CSV – Storage of experiment records.
  • Git and GitHub – Version control and project management.
  • Streamlit Community Cloud – Application deployment.
